subject: hollow bones
title: What If You Had Hollow Bones Like a Bird? You Wouldn't Weigh Any Less

scenes.text: What if your bones were hollow, like a bird's? You wouldn't lose a single kilo.
Since 1683, people have said birds fly because hollow bones make them light. In 2010, a biologist weighed the bones.
A two-ounce songbird and a two-ounce rodent have skeletons that weigh about the same. Bird bones are thin, but they're denser than ours.
Dense bone is stiffer, like a titanium toothpick next to a wooden one. The hollow tube shape resists snapping. That's the real trick.
Your new bones would also be plumbed into your lungs. Birds push air through sacs that reach inside their bones, in one direction, with no pause.
So you'd be exactly as heavy, slightly stiffer, and able to breathe through a broken arm. Still not flying.

description:
What if you had hollow bones like a bird? A 2010 study in Proceedings of the Royal Society B weighed the skulls and limb bones of songbirds, rodents and bats and found bird bones are the densest of the three.
A bird's skeleton weighs about as much as a mammal's of the same size; the hollow, dense tube is stiffer and stronger, not lighter. Birds also run air sacs from their lungs into those bones, giving them one-way airflow, which is why a bird can breathe through a broken bone if its windpipe is blocked.
